prompt:
<inputs>
Ask me for my voiceover (mp3 or wav) and its exact script, pasted as text. If I don't have one, pitch 3 map stories (a war, a voyage, a trade route, how a country was made), each with one surprising true fact, then write a 25-35 s script for me to record, one short sentence per beat. Ask if I have an SFX pack to upload. Then show me the beat list and the camera plan before you render anything.
</inputs>

<direction>
A 1920x1080 Vox-style map explainer. The whole video lives on ONE engraved paper map, and the camera flies across it as the story moves. Collage pieces are pinned to real places: black-and-white halftone cut-outs, yellow paint, felt-marker ink, paper tags and ransom-note letters.
- Palette: board #EFEBE3, ink #1D1C20, ONE accent yellow #EDBD2E, beige sheets #F1EDE4. No other colours, ever. Never a dark background.
- Map engraving:
- Sea: 4 coast-parallel lines at 8/19/32/48 px from the shore, then wavy horizontal lines every 22 px.
- Land: a diagonal hatch every 22 px. The featured region gets a cross-hatch every 13 px.
- Lines: coastline 6 px. Borders 4 px dashed (22 on, 18 off). A dotted graticule every 10°. One compass rose in open sea.
- Labels: engraved place names in letter-spaced Libre Caslon (italic for oceans). No other text is baked into the map.
- The featured region is painted yellow, multiplied at 90% so the hatching shows through, and revealed with a sweep (south→north, 16 frames) on the word that names it.
- Everything animates on twos. Every paper piece "boils" ±1.5 px and ±0.4° every 8 frames. Pieces arrive with a slap (scale 1.1 → 0.98 → 1.0, on twos), never a fade.
- Text only on paper: a title card, yellow tags, notes, ransom letters.
- Title card: top left, beige, 560 px wide, rotated −1.2°, with a small yellow "FIG. 0N" tag. Its serif lines (Libre Caslon, 68 px) type on at 1 letter per frame.
- Notes: Permanent Marker, 58-84 px, lower-case, written on at 1.3 letters per frame.
- Tags: Special Elite, 22-26 px, letter-spaced, on small yellow paper strips.
- Ransom letters: one cut-paper letter slapped down every 3-4 frames, cycling Caslon Bold, Anton and Special Elite on ink, beige and yellow squares.
- Banned: any colour except the palette, photos of real people, logos, burned-in subtitles, glassy UI cards, a frame where nothing moves, and any invented fact.
</direction>

<structure>
Length: the voice decides, plus a 1.3 s hold after the last word. One sentence = one beat. A beat starts 6 frames before its first word.
0 s the home region at zoom ~0.6: it paints yellow on its name, and a ransom number slaps onto it
→ pull out WIDE (~0.32) so both sides of the story fit: a dashed arc between them with a distance tag, and the far party as a cut-out pinned to its capital, circled
→ the causes as arrows across the map, one per clause, each with a dated tag; a cut-out prop travels along the last arrow and lands
→ zoom to the event city (~1.35): the date on the title card, pieces dropping in one by one with ink splash marks, and the big true number in ransom letters with a tag under it
→ the reaction/joke beat at the same spot: a cut-out character, a marker note, an ink circle
→ the next city (~1.15): a dated tag, a document cut-out; on the verb, pull WIDE and fly the document along a dashed trail to the other side
→ the consequence back on the region (~0.7): an ink X per event, in date order, each with a "PLACE YEAR" tag
→ final pull out WIDE: the payoff name in ransom letters over the region, the losing side's cut-out swapped for its sad version with a marker note, and a beige sheet bottom-centre with a bold Caslon line and a ransom payoff word underlined with a yellow highlighter. Hold to the end.
</structure>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, numpy, OpenCV, Pillow and FFmpeg. Fonts from https://github.com/google/fonts (Libre Caslon Text, Permanent Marker, Special Elite, Anton). Tell me anything you installed.
2. Timing:
- Try faster-whisper word timestamps first.
- If the model download is blocked, use ffmpeg silencedetect (−35 dB, 0.15 s) to find the speech spans, map each span to its words from my script, and spread the words inside each span by syllable count.
- The voice starts at frame 4. Every cue is "word ± frames", and repeated words are found by their occurrence number.
3. Map:
- Plot coastlines as hand-written lon/lat vertices. Project equirectangular with longitude scaled by cos(mid-latitude), 7200 px wide.
- Smooth every coast with 3 Chaikin passes. Build 4 mip levels (INTER_AREA) and pick level floor(log2(1/zoom) + 0.15) each frame, so the hatching never shimmers.
4. Camera: keyframes of (frame, lon, lat, zoom), eased with smoothstep, zoom interpolated in log space, stepped on twos. One move every 1-3 sentences, 16-26 frames long. The camera never shows past the map's edge.
5. Collage pieces, drawn fully in code: grayscale shapes with soft shading for characters, props and documents.
- Halftone: a 5 px dot screen at 45°, mixed at 34%, contrast 1.25, plus grain.
- Edge and shadow: a 7 px white scissor edge with a noisy wobble, and a shadow offset (5, 7) px, blurred 6 px, at 32%.
- Documents are engraved line art on cream paper, with no halftone.
- Pin each piece to a lon/lat plus a pixel offset. Pieces keep a constant screen size.
- Movers travel along their arrow's spline with smoothstep and a ±4° wobble.
6. Ink:
- Project the control points to the screen every frame and draw there, so the weight stays 5-6 px at every zoom.
- Felt marker: circles stamped every 1.6 px with a ±15% width wobble and tapered ends, plus a dry crayon pass at 0.32 width with 35% dropouts, merged with max().
- Boil: 3 jitter seeds, cycled every 8 frames.
- Reveal each mark along its own path over 8-15 frames.
- Arrowheads 26 px at ±0.48 rad. Dashes 27 on, 19 off.
- Ink X: two 20 px strokes over 6 frames.
- Highlighter: 26-34 px of yellow, multiplied.
7. Finish: a paper texture multiplied over every frame (cloud noise, fibres, creases, grain, a soft vignette), plus dust specks swapped every 8 frames.
8. Render:
- Draw frames with numpy/OpenCV at 30 fps, split across CPU workers, each piping raw RGB to ffmpeg libx264 CRF 16. Concat the segments.
- Before the full render, show me a 10-12 frame contact sheet. Fix overlaps, empty stretches, text off-frame and blank map edges.
9. Sound:
- Use my SFX pack if I upload one; if not, synthesize: a paper slap for each piece, a marker scratch for each ink mark, typewriter ticks for typed text, a scribble for the yellow reveal, and a soft whoosh on every fast camera move.
- SFX sit at about 0.32 × the voice peak. Merge same-type hits within 3 frames.
- Peak at −0.3 dB, mux as AAC 192k.
</build>

<gotchas>
Smoothing a closed land polygon rounds its corners at the map edge into a fake coastline, so push every closing corner off the canvas first. A shot zoomed onto a coast shows blank board past the map's edge, so draw the map at least 25° beyond any shot. At city zoom 0.2° is only about 16 px, so space pieces with pixel offsets, not degrees. Give every element an end frame, or tags from the last beat collide with the next beat's. Check every pinned note at both of its camera positions, because a note that fits wide can sit off-screen when zoomed in. If the crayon pass overwrites the marker pass instead of using max(), the ink and the yellow go see-through. Size the title card from its line count. Coastlines are approximations, so say so; every date, number and place must be real. Draw no real person's likeness: use generic characters (a king, a colonist, a sailor).
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask for my voiceover and script (or pitch 3 map stories), then show me the beat list and the camera plan.
</start>
